summary: xAI launched Grok Bot, a beta product giving users persistent, tool-using AI agents that operate their own cloud computer across apps and inboxes, coordinate with other agents, and run continuously with minimal human oversight.

mechanisms.reason: The product is explicitly built around agents that execute delegated, multi-step work end-to-end across tools rather than a human operating software directly.
mechanisms.quote: Grok Bot is your team of always-on agents. They have their own computer, work inside tools and apps like you do, and keep working 24/7.

mechanisms.reason: Bots running continuously across many parallel tasks and coordinating with each other implies more inference calls per unit of delegated work, though no volume figures are given.
mechanisms.quote: People inside SpaceXAI often run multiple Bots in parallel, with one to manage the others.

practices.reason: The chief-of-staff-plus-specialist-agents pattern with cross-agent messaging and group-chat coordination is a design an engineering team could imitate, but no implementation detail or measured gain is given.
practices.quote: Instead of multiple agents you have to manage, Grok Bot gives you a small team that can work in parallel so you’re not the middleman. Bots can independently message each other and share context in threads.

practices.reason: New availability tiers and platforms (SuperGrok, Cursor subscriptions, desktop/iOS) define where and how teams could integrate the product, though this creates no urgent migration work.
practices.quote: Grok Bot is in beta and available today for SuperGrok Plus and Heavy, Cursor Pro+ and Ultra, and Cursor Teams Standard and Premium subscribers on desktop and iOS.

notable_reason: It is a first-party launch of a persistent, multi-agent product that operates its own computer across arbitrary apps without APIs, a concrete step in the shift from seat-based software to agent-executed work.
